text:
support-ops: FYI customer CNX-270 reporting big latency spikes and 502s since ~09:10 UTC, says requests are getting routed to ap-southeast even though tenant is pinned to us-west. Escalating, attaching logs we got from the customer.

kevin: +1 seeing a flood of route_fallback events in the routing logs starting 09:09. Looks like health checks for us-west pool returned DOWN and traffic fell back to asia-1.

mara: Can you paste the healthcheck response? Also which probe type are we using for that pool (tcp/tls/http)?

kevin: It's the tls probe hitting :443 with SNI set to service.internal. Sample tcp dump: 
```
09:09:12 -> 10.2.4.9:443 TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed (depth=2)
09:09:12 healthcheck: backend 10.2.4.9:443 status=DOWN reason="TLS verify failed"
```

kevin: Customer curl against the LB IP from their side: `curl -v https://lb-usw1.redwood.example --resolve lb-usw1.redwood.example:443:52.23.11.7` shows `SSL: certificate subject mismatch`

jon: Hmm we rotated the probe certs in us-west at 08:58 as part of the scheduled cert-roll. Probe certs are stored separately from app certs; I need to check if the new cert has correct SANs/SNI.

heartbeat-bot: [09:09:15] healthcheck-down: pool=us-west-primary consecutive_failures=3 threshold=3 -> initiating failover to us-west-backup/regional-fallback:ap-southeast-1

mara: That explains the routing. But the cert rotation should be invisible. Possible causes: cert missing SAN, probe not sending SNI, or the probe requesting `service.internal` while the cert only has `lb-usw1.redwood.example`.

lee: Also noticed previous config change that tightened the healthcheck grace window from 30s -> 6s last week. That makes flapping more likely.

kevin: Repro steps from support (customer environment):
1) `dig lb-usw1.redwood.example +short` -> `52.23.11.7`
2) `curl -v --resolve lb-usw1.redwood.example:443:52.23.11.7 https://lb-usw1.redwood.example/health` -> `SSL: certificate subject "CN=probe.local" does not match 'lb-usw1.redwood.example'`

mara: Confirmed on our side when I hit the probe endpoint from bastion: TLS cert returned `CN=probe.local` (old internal probe cert) not `lb-usw1`. That explains verification failure.

jon: I rolled back the probe cert rotation to the previous cert at 09:22 on nodes in us-west pool. Rolling back should restore healthchecks. I also bumped healthcheck threshold back to 4 for the pool (temporary).

kevin: After rollback heartbeat-bot posted: `healthcheck-up: pool=us-west-primary restored after 2 successful probes` and routing started moving traffic back at 09:26. But customer still saw some cross-region traffic for a few minutes.

dana: Actions we should take (short term):
- Verify cert bundling step in probe rotation job (jon)
- Add SNI sanity check in rotation job to avoid probe certs without proper SANs (mara)
- Increase grace window for all TLS probes from 6s -> 20s to reduce flapping (lee)
- Notify affected customers about incident and mitigation (support-ops)

mara: I'll open a PR to the rotation job: add `openssl x509 -noout -subject -ext subjectAltName` assertions and fail the job if SAN doesn't match expected hostname. Also add an integration test that runs `openssl s_client -connect` against a canary LB before promoting certs.

jon: I'll add a quick patch to the rolling job to preserve the previous cert until final commit, and a heuristic to skip a node if the probe health fails after rotation.

kevin: Support message to customer drafted: "We've identified a probe certificate mismatch during a routine rotation which caused transient healthcheck failures and temporary regional failover. We've rolled back the rotation and traffic is back to us-west. We're updating our probe rotation to prevent recurrence. Apologies for the disruption." Want me to send?

support-ops: Please send, include timeframe and what we changed (rollback + thresholds).

heartbeat-bot: [09:40:12] incident: resolved -> monitoring. Metric: cross_region_p99_latency spike cleared in 10m.

dana: I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If anything else crops up we'll re-open. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lee: Follow-ups: file an infra postmortem wiki (assigned to jon/mara) and schedule a short runbook update for TLS probe rotation.

mara: noted, will start the postmortem skeleton now.

kevin: Closing the ticket on our side after support message sent.

support-ops: Sent to customer at 09:45 UTC. Customer ack'd and said latency normalized.

dana: end state: rollback applied, thresholds bumped, probe-rotation PR open, monitoring green. Marking thread resolved but leaving for follow-up tasks.
